editorial:
Imagine you buy a used laptop and find a hidden folder full of creepy videos. That's exactly what happens to Matias, a young guy who just wants to impress his deaf girlfriend Amaya. He logs into a group video call with his friends to show off his new computer, but things go wrong fast. They stumble onto files showing people being hurt, and soon a mysterious group from the dark web starts watching them. The whole movie plays out on computer screens, which makes it feel like you're right there in the chat. It's tense, scary, and surprisingly clever for a screen-based horror film.

The acting feels natural, like real friends talking over video chat. The pacing keeps you on edge because you never know what will pop up next on screen. On the downside, some characters make dumb choices that might frustrate you, and the ending can feel a bit unfair. Still, if you enjoy found-footage style horror or movies like Searching, this is a fun, creepy watch. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Matias tries to save Amaya by following the dark web group's orders, but it's too late. The group kills his friends one by one and finally kills Amaya too. Matias is left broken, and the laptop's original owner, Charon, gets his computer back. The movie ends with Charon selling the laptop to a new buyer, showing the nightmare will start all over again with someone else.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves screen-based horror and dark web thrillers.
